text: Computer-aided detection for TB screening provides a probability score. A score above the threshold indicates possible TB and the patient should be referred for confirmatory sputum testing such as Xpert MTB/RIF.
TB is treated with a standard 6-month regimen of antibiotics. Treatment must be completed in full even after symptoms improve. Early treatment prevents spread and drug resistance.

A positive screening result means further testing is needed, not that you definitely have TB. TB is curable with proper treatment. Cover your mouth when coughing and attend all follow-up appointments.

Patients with high-probability screening results should be referred promptly for confirmatory testing. Delays in diagnosis increase transmission risk. Xpert MTB/RIF is the recommended first-line confirmatory test.
